simplified.title: Hver synes best om sine barn

english.title: Everyone Loves Their Own Children Best

world: Old rural Norway, long ago, in a forest where the birds can talk. A narrow footpath winds through a light forest of pine, spruce and birch along the edge of a wide, open bog with tufts of white cotton grass, soft moss, low heather, cloudberry plants and small dark pools, with low blue hills far away. The hunter carries an old, long-barrelled muzzle-loading gun. The dunlin is a real, natural bird, no bigger than a starling.
palette: A still July day at the bog: warm midday sunshine that turns to low, golden evening light, with soft dappled shade under the pines, fluffy white cotton grass, ripening orange cloudberries, rusty-red and olive-green bog moss and dark pools reflecting a hazy pale sky.

cast.look: A tall, lean, weather-tanned hunter of about thirty with a long, friendly face, a slightly crooked nose, crinkly grey-blue eyes, a clean-shaven chin and long, straight jet-black hair tied back with a leather thong. He wears a wide-brimmed dark-green hat with a long brown feather, a grey wool jacket with big patch pockets, brown leather knee breeches, red knitted stockings and lace-up boots, with a leather game bag and a small brass hunting horn on cords across his chest, and carries an old long-barrelled gun.
cast.portrait: Background: the footpath along the sunny bog.

simplified.name: Skytteren
simplified.description: En jeger som lover å la de «vakreste» ungene være, men ender med å skyte de han synes er styggest.

english.name: The Hunter
english.description: A practical woodsman whose offhand logic about beauty and ugliness drives the tale’s twist.

cast.look: A small, round-bodied dunlin in summer plumage, about the size of a starling, with a rusty-chestnut back speckled with black, a pale head and breast finely streaked with grey, a big black patch on her white belly, a long, slightly down-curved black beak, thin black legs and bright black eyes. When she spreads her wings, a white stripe shows along each one. A brave, proud little mother.
cast.portrait: Background: white cotton grass on the bog.

simplified.name: Myrsnipe
simplified.description: En fuglemor som trygler om at ungene hennes ikke skal bli skutt, og som tror de er de vakreste i skogen.

english.name: The Snipe
english.description: A small bird and proud mother who insists her chicks are the prettiest in the forest, only to be proven humorously biased.

cover.prompt: Low, close view at the edge of the bog on a still July day: the Dunlin, tiny and proud, stands on a mossy tussock among white cotton grass with her chest puffed out and her head held high, looking very sure of herself. Behind her, further along the footpath at the edge of the pine forest, the Hunter walks with his long gun over his shoulder, not yet noticing her. Warm light and two blue dragonflies.

simplified.caption: Myrsnipa er sikker på at barna hennes er de vakreste i skogen.
simplified.alt: Ei lita myrsnipe står stolt på en mosetue mellom hvit myrull. Lenger bak går en skytter med børsa over skulderen langs skogkanten.

english.caption: The snipe is quite sure her children are the prettiest in the forest.
english.alt: A small snipe stands proudly on a mossy tussock among white cotton grass. Further back, a hunter walks along the edge of the forest with his gun over his shoulder.

illustrations.prompt: On the footpath at the edge of the bog in bright midday sun, the Dunlin stands on a tuft of heather right in front of the Hunter's boots, her wings half spread, her chest puffed out and her head held high, utterly sure of herself. The Hunter has lowered his long gun so that it points at the ground, and he bends forward with raised eyebrows and a surprised, amused face. Pines on one side, white cotton grass on the other.

simplified.anchor: «De vakreste barna som går i skogen, det er mine!»
simplified.caption: «De vakreste barna som går i skogen, det er mine!»
simplified.alt: Ei lita myrsnipe står stolt på en lyngtue rett foran støvlene til skytteren. Skytteren har senket børsa og bøyer seg fram og ser overrasket på henne.

english.anchor: “The prettiest children that walk in the forest are mine!”
english.caption: “The prettiest children that walk in the forest are mine!”
english.alt: A small snipe stands proudly on a tuft of heather right in front of the hunter's boots. The hunter has lowered his gun and leans forward, looking at her in surprise.

illustrations.prompt: Seen from low down at bird height on the footpath at the edge of the bog, in low golden evening light: the small Dunlin stands very straight on a tuft of moss, her head lifted high, calmly answering. In front of her, filling one side of the picture, stand the Hunter's worn lace-up boots, red knitted stockings and leather breeches, seen only from the knees down, with the butt of his long gun resting on the ground. White cotton grass glows in the low sun.

simplified.caption: «Vet du ikke at hver synes best om sine barn?»
simplified.alt: Sett helt nede fra bakken står myrsnipa rank på en mosetue og løfter hodet mot skytteren, som bare synes fra knærne og ned. Myrulla lyser i kveldssola.

english.caption: “Don’t you know that everyone loves their own children best?”
english.alt: Seen from down on the ground, the snipe stands tall on a tuft of moss and lifts her head towards the hunter, who is seen only from the knees down. The cotton grass glows in the evening sun.
